name: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Efferent Suppression Cuff
description:
The Efferent Suppression Cuff is a rigid polymer band, twelve centimeters wide, applied to a limb proximal to a traumatic injury to interrupt motor nerve conduction in the affected region without interrupting sensory or autonomic signaling. Where a conventional tourniquet manages blood loss through mechanical compression, the Cuff manages neurogenic shock and uncontrolled muscular spasm through targeted bioelectric interference — a low-amplitude pulsed field tuned to the efferent nerve frequencies documented in Zheng-Dao's proprietary human neural atlas. The result is a limb that can no longer generate voluntary or involuntary muscular contraction distal to the Cuff, while retaining circulation and sensation. This is particularly valuable in crush injury and blast trauma scenarios, where involuntary muscular activity in a damaged limb can worsen internal bleeding and complicate extraction.

The Cuff's selective interference profile is its defining engineering achievement. Early-generation nerve suppression devices — some of which still circulate in the outer ring — used broadband electrical interference that suppressed all nerve conduction indiscriminately, creating a limb that was numb, pulseless, and increasingly ischemic. Zheng-Dao's efferent-selective approach, refined across four hardware generations, preserves the autonomic signals that regulate vascular tone, preventing the vasoconstriction that caused ischemic complications in earlier devices. The Cuff can be worn for up to four hours without clinically significant nerve damage in healthy tissue; in compromised tissue, Zheng-Dao recommends two hours and documents the rest as acceptable liability.

The device has a civilian medical license in GLMZ's mid-ring districts and is standard equipment in Zheng-Dao's own corporate medical facilities. It also has a significant off-label market: the same efferent suppression field that prevents a trauma patient from thrashing through their own injury can, at modified power settings, be used to incapacitate a limb with surgical precision. This application is not discussed in Zheng-Dao's product documentation, but it is discussed extensively in the parts of the city where the Cuff is known as The Quiet.
base_technologies: Vascular tone maintenance through selective conduction

specifications.fit_range: Adjustable, upper arm 28–48cm circumference / thigh 40–72cm circumference
specifications.field_frequency: Tuned to efferent nerve band (proprietary, 80–140Hz modulated)
specifications.safe_wear_duration: 4 hours healthy tissue / 2 hours recommended compromised tissue
specifications.interface: Single-button activation with LED status ring
specifications.compatibility: Contraindicated with active neural implants in affected limb

tactical_use: Applied proximal to crush injury, blast wound, or traumatic limb damage where involuntary spasm is worsening patient condition or complicating extraction. The medic seats the Cuff against the skin, confirms contact indicators, and activates. The limb distal to the Cuff becomes motorically quiet within eight seconds — the patient can feel the limb and blood continues to flow, but muscular contraction ceases. This allows safe extraction from debris, prevents the patient from interfering with wound management, and reduces metabolic demand on damaged tissue. At modified power settings used off-label, the Cuff can be applied to a resisting or combative subject to incapacitate a limb without causing ischemia — a technique used by corporate security and, more quietly, by individuals who need someone cooperative.
cultural_context: The Efferent Suppression Cuff sits at an uncomfortable intersection of medicine and control in GLMZ. Its legitimate use is well-documented and genuinely valuable, and mid-ring paramedics regard it as an essential tool for complex trauma extraction. Its off-label use — applied by people who are not treating the wearer, to make them easier to manage — is an open secret that Zheng-Dao Bioelectric has never formally acknowledged. The name 'The Quiet' emerged from this dual identity: it is the quiet of a limb that has stopped fighting its own injury, and it is the quiet of a person who no longer has the option to resist. In GLMZ's more candid social spaces, the question of whether those two kinds of quiet are meaningfully different is a recurring argument.
story_hooks: A modified Efferent Suppression Cuff is recovered from the scene of an abduction — its power output has been pushed far beyond the incapacitation range into territory that should have caused permanent nerve damage, but the victim's medical records show no lasting injury. Someone has figured out how to push the ceiling further than Zheng-Dao thought possible.

A mid-ring paramedic is being investigated after a patient she treated with the Cuff reported that the device remained active and locked after she left the scene. The paramedic insists she deactivated it. Someone remotely re-engaged it.

Zheng-Dao's neural atlas — the proprietary frequency map that makes the Cuff's selectivity possible — has been leaked in fragments. Someone is using it to build something that is not a medical device.

A fixer is hired to retrieve a Cuff that was left on a client who has since gone to ground. The device is still active. The client has been immobile for longer than the two-hour compromised-tissue threshold.

physical_description.visual_profile: A rigid polymer cuff band, clinical and geometric in design. The primary surface is a smooth, slightly curved cylindrical form that wraps around a limb. Internally visible through transparent side panels are dense arrays of contact points and copper trace circuitry. The aesthetic is utilitarian medical—neither organic nor decorative, but precisely engineered for function.
physical_description.dimensions: 12cm wide band; adjustable circumference 28–48cm (arm) or 40–72cm (thigh); forms a complete ring when fastened
physical_description.weight_description: 190g total; light enough for one-handed application, worn as a sleeve or upper-thigh band
physical_description.primary_material: Medical-grade rigid polymer (matte charcoal gray), with transparent polycarbonate side panels exposing internal bioelectric circuitry
physical_description.finish: Matte non-reflective polymer body; interior contact points have a brushed copper finish; transparent panels show anodized aluminum support structure
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with copper/bronze accent traces visible through side panels; white LED status ring at anterior surface
physical_description.interface_elements: Single large circular activation button (pressure-sensitive, white surround with LED backlight) at center-front; full-circumference status LED ring that cycles through green (standby), amber (active), and red (fault); small Zheng-Dao logo stamp and regulatory certification marks on outer surface; adjustment clasp with numbered sizing dial
distinctive_features: Transparent polycarbonate side panels revealing internal copper trace networks and bioelectric contact arrays
Continuous LED status ring that provides 360-degree visibility of device state
Anatomically curved interior with embedded contact electrode grid visible as regular copper dimples
Numbered adjustment dial with detent positions for rapid sizing
Integrated graphene cell housing visible as slight bulge on one side panel
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC embossed on outer surface; regulatory stamps for GLMZ mid-ring medical certification; proprietary neural tuning data encoded as subtle laser-etched QR on inner band
physical_description.condition_typical: Clinical and pristine in retail; in-field use shows wear on adjustment clasp and potential discoloration on inner contact surface from skin contact; older units may show slight transparency cloudiness on panels from repeated sterilization cycles
